title: Bind purposes, audiences, and dispositions independently
summary: Represent who a matter concerns and why without assigning global importance. Several audiences and objectives can share evidence while receiving different consequences and treatments.
implementation: Define independent purpose and audience revisions with effective intervals and responsibility scopes.
Bind assessments to the context components they consume.
Implement acknowledgement, deferral, rejection, and decision dispositions with authority and supersession.
Expose dependencies so delivery preference changes cannot reclassify unchanged facts.

acceptance.criterion: One matter supports different treatments with a shared evidence assessment.
acceptance.verification: Evaluate observer and responsible-actor audiences over fixed evidence.

acceptance.criterion: A disposition applies only within its declared scope and period.
acceptance.verification: Test deferral expiry and an unrelated audience.

acceptance.criterion: Context changes preserve matter identity and old assessment bindings.
acceptance.verification: Change active objective and inspect historical references.

tests: A host agent can own the next action while the human stays quiet.
Rejecting one proposal does not reject all future evidence.
Acknowledgement does not imply agreement or repair.
risks: Broad disposition keys can suppress new developments or unrelated audiences.

reuse.application: Implement purpose/audience-specific assessments and independent delivery preferences.

evidence: 2026-10-27: Independent versioned contexts and scoped dispositions preserve shared evidence, exact original targets, expiry, withdrawal and historical bindings. Actual acceptance evidence and limitations: docs/validation/MAT-018.md.
